literal: He followed the imperial campaign against Liu Yilong, reaching the Yangtze.
idiomatic: He rode with the imperial host against Liu Yilong as far as the Yangtze.

literal: His title was advanced to Duke of Nankang; he was given the additional rank General Who Champions the State and died in the army.
idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Nankang, made general who champions the state, and died on campaign.

literal: His son Wu'er inherited the enfeoffment.
idiomatic: His son Wu'er inherited the fief.

literal: At the opening of Gaozu's reign he was palace attendant and garrison commandant of Wuchuan.
idiomatic: When Gaozu began his reign he served as palace attendant and commandant of the Wuchuan garrison.

literal: At the opening of the Taihe era he died; posthumously made Inspector of Hengzhou.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Taihe era he died and was posthumously named inspector of Hengzhou.

literal: His son Changle succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Changle succeeded.

literal: For an offense his enfeoffment was revoked.
idiomatic: For an offense his title was stripped away.

literal: Later he held the posts of General of Lingjiang and Superintendent of the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: Later he served as general of Lingjiang and superintendent of the Feathered Forest.

literal: His son Rongzu, in the Wuding era, was General Who Campaigns West and Baron of Fanchang.
idiomatic: His son Rongzu, in the Wuding era, was general who campaigns west and baron of Fanchang.

literal: Wu'er's younger brother Tu was chief clerk of Shuozhou.
idiomatic: Wu'er's younger brother Tu was chief clerk of Shuozhou, the record states.

literal: His son Yuanqing was registrar of the granary office in Pingzhou.
idiomatic: His son Yuanqing was registrar of the granary office in Pingzhou.

literal: Wei Guzhen was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Wei Guzhen came from Dai.

literal: When Taizu was among the Helan tribes, He Rangan sent Houyin Yitu and others to the mobile palace intending treason.
idiomatic: While Taizu still lived among the Helan, He Rangan sent Houyin Yitu and others to the traveling palace to plot rebellion.

literal: Guzhen learned of it and secretly reported by swift messenger; Houyin and the rest did not dare act.
idiomatic: Guzhen learned of the plot and sent word in secret; Houyin and his party never dared move.

literal: Rangan suspected Guzhen had leaked the plot, seized him and beat him with the cudgel, pressing two chariot axles against his head and injuring one eye; he would not confess and was therefore released.
idiomatic: Rangan, suspecting Guzhen had betrayed him, had him seized and beaten with the cudgel; two chariot axles were pressed to his head and one eye was ruined, yet he would not confess and was let go.

literal: At the opening of Dengguo he followed campaigns against the Kumo Xi and Chitulin, both with merit.
idiomatic: When the Dengguo era opened he marched against the Kumo Xi and Chitulin and won merit in both.

literal: He also followed the relief of Helan, defeated Wei Chen's son Zhilidi, and again struck Murong Bao at Canhe Slope.
idiomatic: He also rode to relieve Helan, broke Wei Chen's son Zhilidi, and struck Murong Bao again at Canhe Slope.

literal: He again followed the pacification of the central plains; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dongzhou and made commissioner bearing the Staff of Authority.
idiomatic: He marched again in the conquest of the central plains; merit made him Marquis of Dongzhou and commissioner with the staff of authority.

literal: At the opening of Taizong's reign he was General of Soaring Flight, leading five thousand men to garrison Daluo city.
idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he was General of Soaring Flight, commanding five thousand men at Daluo.

literal: On Taizong's western tour, Guzhen with Xi Jin and others led the vanguard to chastise the Yuele tribe,[2] routing them utterly; they took fifty thousand horses, two hundred thousand head of cattle and sheep, and drove more than twenty thousand families west in plunder.
idiomatic: On Taizong's western progress Guzhen and Xi Jin led the van against the Yuele tribe[2] and shattered them, taking fifty thousand horses, two hundred thousand cattle and sheep, and herding more than twenty thousand households west as booty.

literal: In the third year of Taichang he was made Inspector of Dingzhou.
idiomatic: In Taichang year 3 he was named inspector of Dingzhou.

literal: He died; his son Yiwani inherited.
idiomatic: He died; his son Yiwani succeeded.

literal: He died; his son Sheng inherited.
idiomatic: He died; his son Sheng succeeded.

literal: Guzhen's younger brother Taizhen, at the opening of Taizong's reign, was General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: Guzhen's younger brother Taizhen, when Taizong took power, was general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiangzhou.

literal: Taizhen's younger brother Nuo, in youth attending Taizu, was famed for loyalty and prudence.
idiomatic: Taizhen's younger brother Nuo had attended Taizu from boyhood and was famed for loyal care.

literal: In the siege of Zhongshan, Nuo was first up the wall and lost an eye.
idiomatic: At the siege of Zhongshan Nuo was first over the wall and lost an eye.

literal: Taizu sighed and said: "Nuo and his brothers have each ruined an eye to build achievement—truly praiseworthy.
idiomatic: Taizu sighed and said, "The Nuo brothers have each cost an eye in service—worthy of praise indeed.

literal: " Favor and attendance then rose greatly.
idiomatic: " Honor and favor followed in full measure.

literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed Viscount of Anle.
idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the east and enfeoffed as viscount of Anle.

literal: Following the campaign against Yao Ping, on his return he was appointed Grandee of the National Tribes.
idiomatic: After the campaign against Yao Ping he returned and was named grandee of the national tribes.

literal: At the opening of Taizong's reign he was Inspector of Youzhou, with the added title General of Eastern Command, and his enfeoffment advanced to marquis.
idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he was inspector of Youzhou, given the added rank general of eastern command, and raised to marquis.

literal: In Changsun Daosheng's campaign against Feng Ba, Nuo with the Valiant Cavalry General Yan Pu led troops stationed in Liaoxi.
idiomatic: When Changsun Daosheng marched against Feng Ba, Nuo and the Valiant Cavalry General Yan Pu held the line in Liaoxi.

literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and his title advanced to Duke of Wuling.
idiomatic: He was moved to general who pacifies the east and advanced to Duke of Wuling.

literal: While Nuo held the province he had benevolent rule; officials and commoners cherished his memory.
idiomatic: In his years in the province Nuo governed with kindness; officials and people alike kept his memory.

literal: In Shizu's time more than two hundred men of Ji, including Zhang Guangda, came to court to request him; he was again made General Who Establishes the East and Inspector of Youzhou, with his fief changed to Duke of Liaoxi.
idiomatic: Under Shizu more than two hundred men of Ji, Zhang Guangda among them, came to court to ask for him back; he was again named general who establishes the east and inspector of Youzhou, with his fief changed to Duke of Liaoxi.

literal: The brothers alike became frontier governors—a glory of their day.
idiomatic: Brothers alike held frontier commanderies—a glory of their age.

literal: The Yan region had long been in disorder and households scattered; in his ten-odd years in the province Nuo brought back more than ten thousand families to their livelihood.
idiomatic: Yan had been torn by years of disorder and empty villages; in a decade or more in office Nuo brought more than ten thousand households back to their fields.

literal: He died in the Yanhe era.
idiomatic: He died in the Yanhe era, the record states.

literal: His eighth son Guan[3] inherited the title.
idiomatic: His eighth son Guan[3] inherited the title, the record states.

literal: He died; his son Lun inherited.
idiomatic: He died; his son Lun succeeded.

literal: Juan was also made General Who Pacifies the North and went out to garrison the northern marches.
idiomatic: Juan was also named general who pacifies the north and sent to hold the northern marches.

literal: With the Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han he struck the Rouran splinter chief Afugan at Zuo Mountain; he led the army to Geshan mountain and struck the Rouran splinter chief Biandu's younger brother Kurenzhi, then drew the host north.
idiomatic: With the Prince of Pingyang, Changsun Han, he fell on the Rouran lieutenant Afugan at Zuo Mountain, then marched to Geshan and struck Biandu's younger brother Kurenzhi before turning the army north.

literal: The Rouran tribal chief Mogao led five thousand Gaoche horse to oppose him; Juan routed them and took heads numbering more than a thousand.
idiomatic: The Rouran chief Mogao came against him with five thousand Gaoche riders; Juan broke them and took more than a thousand heads.

literal: He again followed a campaign against the Rouran.
idiomatic: He marched again against the Rouran.

literal: Juan ranged between the white and black deserts and struck their eastern division, taking a great booty and returning.
idiomatic: Juan ranged between the white and black deserts, struck the eastern Rouran, and came home with heavy spoils.

literal: He again followed the campaign against Helian Chang; Juan took the southern route and struck Chang at Shanggui.
idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Helian Chang; Juan took the southern road and struck Chang at Shanggui.

literal: Soldiers and multitudes lacked grain; the Duke of Linhuai Qiu Dui and others levied grain rents in the commanderies and counties and were defeated by Chang.
idiomatic: The army ran short of grain; the Duke of Linhuai, Qiu Dui, and others gathered rents in the commanderies and were beaten by Chang.

literal: Chang pressed his victory in raiding and plunder; the generals were all worried.
idiomatic: Chang pressed his victory in raids and plunder, and the commanders grew uneasy.

literal: Juan with Attending Censor An Pi secretly set an ambush, intercepted and captured Chang.
idiomatic: Juan and the attending censor An Pi laid an ambush in secret, intercepted Chang, and took him alive.

literal: For merit he was made General Who Pacifies the North, added Palace Attendant, and his title advanced to Duke of Yuyang.
idiomatic: Merit made him general who pacifies the north and palace attendant, and his title rose to Duke of Yuyang.

literal: [4] Later he followed the campaign against Helong; Juan directed ten thousand riders as vanguard and soothed more than two thousand surrendering households.
idiomatic: [4] Later, on the Helong campaign, Juan led ten thousand horse as vanguard and won over more than two thousand surrendering households.

literal: Soon he held credential staff as acting commissioner, was added Palace Attendant, and as commander supervised military affairs in Yu and Luo and within Henei; he was General Who Pacifies the South, opened a bureau, and garrisoned Hubao.
idiomatic: Soon he bore the staff as acting commissioner, was added palace attendant, and as commander oversaw armies in Yu, Luo, and Henei; he was general who pacifies the south, opened a bureau, and held Hubao.

literal: When Tufa Baozhou, Prince of Zhangye, rebelled, Juan was summoned with Prince of Yongchang Jian and others to lead troops against him, routing Baozhou at Fanhe.
idiomatic: When Tufa Baozhou, Prince of Zhangye, rebelled, Juan was called up with the Prince of Yongchang, Jian, and others; they broke Baozhou at Fanhe.

literal: Baozhou fled; Juan led cavalry in pursuit until Baozhou, driven to extremity, killed himself.
idiomatic: Baozhou fled; Juan rode after him until, cornered, Baozhou took his own life.

literal: An edict ordered Juan to remain and garrison Liangzhou, with added command of military affairs in Liang, Sha, and He provinces as General Who Pacifies the West and as protector of the Qiang and Rong.
idiomatic: An edict left Juan to garrison Liangzhou, with added command of Liang, Sha, and He armies as general who pacifies the west and protector of the Qiang and Rong.

literal: He was transferred to garrison commissioner of Dunhuang.
idiomatic: He was moved to garrison commissioner of Dunhuang.

literal: He again routed the Tuyuhun and took more than three thousand captives.
idiomatic: He routed the Tuyuhun again and took more than three thousand captives.

literal: Juan successively garrisoned the four frontiers; his martial name was famed everywhere.
idiomatic: Juan held the four marches in turn; his martial name stood out in every quarter.

literal: In Gaozong's time he led troops north to strike Yiwu, took its city, and returned with a great haul.
idiomatic: Under Gaozong he marched north against Yiwu, took the city, and returned laden with spoils.

literal: Soon he was made Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant and his title advanced to prince.
idiomatic: Soon he was palace attendant and grand commandant, and his title rose to prince.

literal: With the Grand Preceptor Chang Ying and others he reviewed Masters of Writing affairs.
idiomatic: With the grand preceptor Chang Ying and others he reviewed affairs in the Masters of Writing.

literal: On Gaozong's northern imperial hunt, as cold snow was about to fall, there was discussion of turning back.
idiomatic: On Gaozong's northern hunt, as bitter snow threatened, the court talked of turning back.

literal: Juan remonstrated: "Now having moved a great host to overawe the northern enemy, we are not far from the capital—yet if we wheel the imperial carriage, the barbarians will surely suspect we have internal trouble.
idiomatic: Juan remonstrated: "We have moved a great host to overawe the northern foe and are not far from the capital—yet if we wheel the imperial carriage now, the barbarians will surely think we have trouble within.

literal: Though snow is now bitter and troops suffer hardship, for the larger strategy of state we ought to press forward.
idiomatic: Snow is bitter and the troops suffer, but for the larger strategy of state we ought to press on.

literal: " Gaozong followed this and crossed the desert on the return.
idiomatic: " Gaozong took his counsel and crossed the desert on the homeward march.

literal: As a senior elder Juan was granted staff and shoes to ascend the hall.
idiomatic: As a senior elder Juan was granted staff and shoes to enter the hall.

literal: In the fourth year of Heping he died.
idiomatic: He died in Heping year 4.

literal: Gaozong mourned him and posthumously made him Grand General with posthumous title Zhuang.
idiomatic: Gaozong mourned him and posthumously named him grand general with the posthumous title Zhuang.

literal: His son Duohou inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Duohou succeeded him the title.

literal: Duohou in youth had martial ability; in Xianzu's time he was acting commissioner, General Who Campaigns West, protector of the Qiang and Rong, and garrison commissioner of Dunhuang.
idiomatic: Duohou in youth showed martial talent; under Xianzu he was acting commissioner, general who campaigns west, protector of the Qiang and Rong, and garrison commissioner of Dunhuang.

literal: On reaching his post he memorialized asking to lead five thousand light cavalry west into Khotan to subdue the various states in passing, taking supplies from the enemy and achieving pacification.
idiomatic: On reaching his post he asked leave to lead five thousand light horse west into Khotan, subduing the western states as he went and feeding his men from the enemy until the region was pacified.

literal: It was not granted.
idiomatic: The throne did not grant it.

literal: At the opening of Gaozu's reign the Rouran tribal chief Jiluzhen led thirty thousand cavalry into the borders to besiege the garrison; Duohou struck and drove them off; for merit his title was advanced to Grand General Who Campaigns West.
idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession the Rouran chief Jiluzhen led thirty thousand horse into the borders to besiege the garrison; Duohou struck and drove them off, and merit raised him to grand general who campaigns west.

literal: Later Duohou was hunting on the southern mountains when the Rouran sent the tribal chief Duba to surround Dunhuang and cut his line of return.
idiomatic: Later, while Duohou hunted the southern mountains, the Rouran sent the chief Duba to surround Dunhuang and cut off his return.

literal: Duohou fought advancing by turns and burst through the encirclement to enter.
idiomatic: Duohou fought as he advanced and broke through the ring into the city.

literal: He led the multitude out to battle, routed them utterly, pursued north several tens of li, and took heads numbering more than a thousand.
idiomatic: He led his men out, routed them utterly, pursued north for tens of li, and took more than a thousand heads.

literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial asking to take Yiwu in the north and sever the Rouran route to the Western Regions.
idiomatic: He then memorialized to seize Yiwu in the north and cut the Rouran road to the Western Regions.

literal: Gaozu approved the plan but, with eastern works then rising, found it difficult.
idiomatic: Gaozu approved the plan, but with eastern works then rising, could not carry it out.

literal: In the first year of Taihe he was killed by his wife, Lady Yuan.
idiomatic: In Taihe year 1 his wife, Lady Yuan, killed him.

literal: His son Jian inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Jian succeeded him the title.

literal: He held office as attendant.
idiomatic: He served as attendant.

literal: He died without sons.
idiomatic: He died without sons, the record states.

literal: Jian's younger brother Na inherited the title.
idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Na inherited the title, the record states.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He passed away.

literal: His son Fan inherited.
idiomatic: His son Fan succeeded.

literal: Fan's younger brother Xianye was Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Xianye was regular attendant.

literal: He committed adultery with the Princess of Taiyuan and begot the son Yan.
idiomatic: He lay with the Princess of Taiyuan and fathered a son, Yan.

literal: In the Wuding era he was General of the Guard and Inspector of Nanyingzhou.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was general of the guard and inspector of Nanyingzhou.

literal: Duohou's younger brother's son Qingbin was skilled in mounted archery and had generalship.
idiomatic: Duohou's nephew Qingbin was skilled in mounted archery and showed commander's gifts.

literal: In Gaozu's time he doffed the hemp and was made Outside-the-Gates Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Casual Staff, then gradually rose to Left General and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: Under Gaozu he doffed the hemp and became outside-the-gates attendant-in-ordinary on the casual staff, then rose by degrees to left general and grand master of splendid happiness.

literal: In Suzong's time, when there was debate on sending the Rouran ruler Anagui back to his country, Qingbin memorialized in firm opposition; the court did not follow.
idiomatic: Under Suzong, when the court debated sending the Rouran ruler Anagui home, Qingbin memorialized in firm opposition; the throne would not listen.

literal: Later the Rouran indeed seized the touring commissioner Yuan Fu and ravaged the northern frontier.
idiomatic: The Rouran then seized the touring commissioner Yuan Fu and ravaged the northern marches.

literal: An edict ordered Minister of Writing Li Chong to chastise them; Qingbin as a detached commander served under Chong, went beyond the passes, and returned.
idiomatic: An edict set the Minister of Writing Li Chong to chastise them; Qingbin served under him as detached commander, went beyond the passes, and came back.

literal: At Yuan Faseng's defection to the outside Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Zong to garrison Xuzhou; an edict also made Qingbin a detached commander under Prince of Anfeng Yanming to chastise him.
idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng defected, Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Zong, to hold Xuzhou; an edict also made Qingbin detached commander under the Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, to strike him.

literal: Soon he was made Rear General and Inspector of Sizhou.
idiomatic: Soon he was rear general and inspector of Sizhou.

literal: At that time Erzhu Rong's military prestige was gradually growing; he once passed through Sizhou, and Qingbin, fearing and loathing him, shut the city and would not come out.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong's military fame was then rising; passing through Sizhou once, he found Qingbin so fearful and hostile that the city gates stayed shut.

literal: Rong hated Qingbin and raised troops to assault him.
idiomatic: Rong hated Qingbin and raised troops to take him.

literal: Qingbin's aide Yao He colluded within; Rong then killed Qingbin's staff, seized Qingbin and brought him back to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."
idiomatic: Qingbin's aide Yao He opened the gates from within; Rong killed Qingbin's staff, seized Qingbin, and carried him to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."

literal: Later, on returning to the capital for his mother's mourning, he was soon recalled and made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and commander, garrisoning Ruyin.
idiomatic: Later, after mourning his mother in the capital, he was soon recalled as general who pacifies the east, grand master of splendid happiness, and commander at Ruyin.

literal: He returned to court and died in the second year of Yong'an.
idiomatic: He returned to court and died in Yong'an year 2.
